status_vocabulary.open: The exact finding remains and must be migrated or explicitly allowlisted.
status_vocabulary.resolved_pending_verification: The static finding disappeared but its owning behavior check has not closed it.
status_vocabulary.closed: The finding is absent and the owning focused behavior verification is recorded.
status_vocabulary.unregistered: The scanner found a current hit that is not yet in this register.

decision_vocabulary.migrate: Remove or replace the pattern under the owning TPQ.
decision_vocabulary.allowlist: Keep the exact finding with a specific reason, risk owner and review date.

Application code manually adds tenant_id predicates or payload ownership
Tenant-owned JOIN condition omits the tenant_id ownership equality
Logic or Controller directly uses Db/PDO/query/prepare
Business code uses page() instead of the shared paginator contract
Accessor/mutator performs a database query
Repository repeats Module availability checks
Application entry bypasses the shared ModuleExecutionBoundary
Known Tenant-owned ORM model does not use TenantOwnedModel
Application code bypasses Model write hooks with insertAll
Generator emits a naked BaseModel, static Logic or manual page query
Application code treats PageResult as an array
Controller calls dataLists with decomposed pagination arguments
A loop performs a query or persistence operation and requires N+1 or batch-write review
Application code manually starts, commits or rolls back a transaction
Model accessor or mutator requires an explicit cast, DTO or presentation decision
Code passes Request to a Tenant context accessor that reads CurrentExecutionContext
Controller constructs a Tenant-aware validator instead of using the shared validation boundary
Application code directly renders a failure response outside the exception renderer
A legacy Logic class remains beside the Application Service boundary
Controller constructs application infrastructure instead of receiving a container binding
Middleware writes dynamic state onto Request
Application code uses an unreviewed direct log, cache or session facade
Provider or business code constructs curl or an HTTP client outside the shared transport
Command or task handler requires registered execution context, retry, idempotency and cleanup ownership
The root route registry still owns Module and identity-specific route declarations
Runtime code obtains another database connection outside the single composition root
Application, service or Module provider code locates dependencies through global app()
A runtime dependency permits a nullable PDO and silently locates or substitutes a connection
Application orchestration performs a raw database query or mutation
Raw database access bypasses the registered Model owner for a table
A generic CLI base forces database construction for commands that do not use persistence
Common code imports or constructs a concrete application Module
Host business code imports a Module Application, Infrastructure or Model implementation instead of its Contracts
Application orchestration imports or branches on a ThinkORM Model or ThinkPHP Console
Application or Module Contracts expose ThinkPHP UploadedFile
Application orchestration constructs a service, factory, transport, gateway, provider or client dependency instead of receiving it
Controller catches Throwable or base Exception instead of using the host problem renderer
Model resolves a dependency through the global application container
A Common business service uses the ThinkPHP database Facade outside an explicit adapter
Service or driver propagates a business failure through mutable getError/setError state
Application or service code locates runtime configuration, environment or HTTP request state outside an explicit boundary
Application or service code assembles a stateful runtime through a zero-argument static factory
A classified authentication, scheduler, payment or persistence error is collapsed to false

issues.reason: Each file key is an independent external storage object and the active StorageDriver contract has no bulk-delete API. The database selection is completed before the loop, so query count is constant; only the required object-store side effects remain per item.

Each pending refund requires an independent provider status query; the per-record database transaction intentionally minimizes lock duration and rechecks current state before applying the idempotent result.

After the external Provider query, the per-refund transaction must re-read and lock the record, latest log and order before applying one idempotent state transition; batching across independent refunds would widen locks and weaken the stale-result guard.
